paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the relationship between computational cost and training loss for two language model approaches. The x-axis represents TFLOPs, displayed on a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to approximately 1.2 × 10⁹, with tick marks at intervals of 0.25 × 10⁹. The y-axis represents Loss, also on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05.

The purple line with triangle markers, labeled "Vanilla," begins at approximately (0.05 × 10⁹, 2.75) and decreases in a generally convex fashion, passing through roughly (0.50 × 10⁹, 2.60) and (0.75 × 10⁹, 2.56), before continuing to decline to approximately (1.20 × 10⁹, 2.50) at the rightmost point. The red line with circle markers, labeled "SepLLM," starts at approximately (0.05 × 10⁹, 2.74) and also decreases, but follows a lower trajectory than the purple line for most of the x-axis range. It passes through roughly (0.25 × 10⁹, 2.60), (0.50 × 10⁹, 2.545), and (0.75 × 10⁹, 2.53), continuing to decrease to approximately (1.20 × 10⁹, 2.475). A green dashed horizontal line is drawn at a loss value of 2.50, and green dashed vertical lines mark the TFLOPs values at which each method reaches this loss level — approximately 0.925 × 10⁹ for SepLLM and approximately 1.18 × 10⁹ for Vanilla. A green annotation with a double-headed arrow between these two vertical dashed lines indicates a factor of 1.28× difference in computational cost to reach the same loss of 2.50.
